rationale: PY-D19 (round 10), the ANALYZER-SIDE half: the fact `from M import *` is a wildcard must SURVIVE to the verdict, and the name it can bind must NOT be invented as a symbol. Both halves are pinned here because they are the two ways this round could be wrong in opposite directions — a dropped fact excuses nothing, and an invented symbol claims a resolution python never made. WHY THE FACT NEEDS A HOME: `from M import *` and `import M` publish the same import-graph endpoint (`M:*`), and the store's per-item projection (`pool-worker`: `{name, path, type, isExternal, line}`) flattens both to `name: "*", type: "namespace"` — so the one difference that decides whether a bare name in this file can come from M's namespace is dropped one layer below the analyzer. It is stated on the edge the analyzer itself returned (`metadata.starImport`), where `python-endpoint-resolution.ts` reads it, exactly as PY-D13 states the bound alias of an aliased import on the same surface. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: `make_dataclass` gets NO symbol. The price for this mechanism (`.tmp-py/price-star-round9.py`) is 171 residual rows whose EVERY star module is out of view, and none of them is resolved — they are DECLARED external by the verdict's new axis, which is why the fixture also pins that the round does not smuggle in a declaration. `os.path.join` is the CONTRAST row: a member call through a module this file imported has a statically known route and keeps `external-member-call`, so the star machinery is not applied to shapes it does not own. Lines and reason codes are measured against the analyzer's own output (`.tmp-py/fixture-shapes-round10.mts`).

expectRelationships.note: THE FACT THE ROUND ADDS. Without this key the verdict cannot tell a wildcard import from a namespace import, and the whole axis is unreachable — which is why the mutant that drops the key must fail here.

THE CONTROL. `import os` binds ONLY `os` and must keep publishing its bare row with no star marker — this row is what makes the star marker a statement about one construct rather than about imports in general.

The corpus shape this axis was priced on (cython's deliberate `from dataclasses import *` test, `make_dataclass`/`astuple`/`asdict`). The analyzer keeps publishing the call with the honest 'a bare name I cannot bind' reason code; the VERDICT is where the wildcard route is declared, and this row pins that the division of labour did not move.
The contrast: `os.path.join` is reachable through this file's own import edge, so it keeps its own declared-external code and must not acquire anything from the star axis.
